tracks.scope: Adversarial review of the M1 reference accessibility core, its declared boundaries, tests and track records.
findings: The deterministic reference core and tests provide useful bounded correctness evidence.
Real road, walking, cycling and timetable engines, national-scale measurements and user-workflow qualification remain open; the evidence does not support M6 or operational accessibility claims.

tracks.scope: Adversarial review of the canonical inventory, schema and ontology implementation, conformance evidence and migration boundaries.
findings: The canonical contracts and local conformance evidence are coherent for the current M1 slice.
A qualifying SHACL report, non-Python round trip, publication identifier, migration matrix and final semantic agent-panel disposition remain unresolved.

tracks.scope: Adversarial review of bounded capture, retry, DNS and runtime evidence at M1.
findings: Retry and capture behavior has executable local evidence, including bounded adverse-path tests.
The track remains specified at M1; representative connector breadth, long-running hosted operation and stable support evidence are not established.

tracks.scope: Adversarial review of the documentation and developer-experience contract and present track evidence.
findings: The track records a coherent documentation scope and agent-panel review boundary.
External user and operator workflows, install and troubleshooting studies, supported-environment evidence and M6 documentation qualification remain unperformed.

tracks.scope: Adversarial review of the synthetic and regional public-source emergency-facilities pilot evidence.
findings: The non-operational synthetic fixture and bounded public-source observations are appropriately labelled and reproducible.
No national authoritative ambulance-station workload, calibrated dispatch or handover model, operational safety evidence or representative stress qualification is present.

tracks.scope: Adversarial review of the small-instance facility-location reference solver and evidence boundaries.
findings: Small deterministic instances provide a credible correctness oracle for the supported formulations.
Scalable solver adapters, interchangeable certificates, national workloads, cost envelopes and independent external benchmark execution remain open.

tracks.scope: Adversarial review of bounded public-source facility reconciliation and conflict-preservation evidence.
findings: The reference implementation preserves source identity and conflict rather than silently adjudicating candidates.
External operator reproduction, national authoritative ambulance coverage, complete supermarket-source evidence, reviewed performance estimates and stable release authority remain open.

tracks.scope: Adversarial review of architecture decisions, governance contracts, roadmap machinery and current validating evidence.
findings: The architecture, release policy, ownership contracts and roadmap validation form a coherent M1 foundation.
The validating status is appropriate; named accountable promotion, complete cross-track qualification, external reproduction and stable operational evidence are not established.

tracks.scope: Adversarial review of the bounded rights, privacy, safety, correction and scope-triggered governance framework.
findings: Fail-closed governance records and correction, withdrawal and publication controls have bounded executable evidence.

The track identifier is historical; current requirements make cultural or community engagement scope-triggered and do not claim live co-design or Māori approval. This panel cannot grant governance authority for a future governed dataset or release.

tracks.scope: Adversarial review of causal-method contracts and synthetic difference-in-differences reference evidence.
findings: The protocol schema and synthetic reference calculations state causal and non-operational limitations.
Empirical public-data analysis, spatial-confounding and MAUP sensitivity, missing-data workflow, preregistration and final methods qualification remain open.

tracks.scope: Adversarial review of Python and Node conformance plus bounded related-repository adapter evidence.
findings: The shared corpus and adapter reports provide useful cross-runtime M1 conformance evidence.
The evidence does not establish full SDK breadth, stable compatibility, external consumer adoption or all M6 standards projections.

tracks.scope: Adversarial review of publication binding, attestations, preserved real-input slices and research-object preparation.
findings: The M1 publication and attestation controls bind methods and bounded evidence without presenting templates as completed releases.
Complete real research objects, final signed attestations, long-term preservation and supported-release verification remain open.

tracks.scope: Adversarial review of the sharded archive contract and bounded LINZ/public real-slice evidence.
findings: The pipeline, fixity checks and bounded real slice support the declared M1 archive reference behavior.
The slice is not a complete national archive and does not establish recurring acquisition, preservation service durability or M6 operational support.

tracks.scope: Adversarial review of resumable archive operations, budgeting and reconciliation behavior.
findings: Local tests cover bounded resume, inventory and budget behavior.
Repeated hosted operation, representative failures, production restore, SLO history, cost history and long-term preservation evidence remain absent.

tracks.scope: Adversarial review of catalogue, enrichment, inventory and source-registry controls.
findings: The registry pipeline preserves explicit source identity and fail-closed disposition for the bounded catalogue slice.
Complete national source coverage, recurring freshness evidence, source change migration and stable operational ownership remain unproven.

tracks.scope: Adversarial review of SRE preparation, hosted technical-preview receipts and elapsed-evidence campaign machinery.
findings: The daily workflow, qualification epochs, lane-specific cumulative ledger, bounded-gap checks, cycle count and digest chain fail closed more reliably than the earlier rehearsal design.

Elapsed 90-day beta and 30-day frozen-RC clocks have not completed; hosted technical-preview recovery is not production disaster recovery, and artifact continuity remains dependent on successful scheduled runs.

tracks.scope: Adversarial review of resource-envelope preparation, scale smoke tests, hosted-runner options and benchmark library choices.
findings: The small-instance correctness oracle and hosted scale smoke are suitable rehearsal evidence, and deferring unused benchmark dependencies avoids needless audit surface.
No authoritative national workload, national ingestion or optimisation measurement, representative cost envelope, stress run or completed soak exists.

tracks.scope: Adversarial review of the bounded WCC plan source pair and spatial-to-rule linkage contract.
findings: The bounded source pair preserves citations and legal-status limitations.
Two materially different councils, quantified false and missing link samples, stable identifiers across plan changes and final agent-panel qualification remain outstanding.

tracks.scope: Adversarial review of transition schemas, golden fixtures and migration playbook.
findings: The implementation makes effective dates and predecessor-successor uncertainty explicit for synthetic fixtures.
Real authority reorganisation and plan-replacement reconstructions, public-source capture and planning-domain qualification remain pending.

tracks.scope: Adversarial review of the provenance profile mapping, validation contract and current conformance evidence.
findings: The mapping inventory distinguishes exact, approximate, preserved, conflicting and unmapped semantics and avoids destructive rewriting of native evidence.
Non-Python validator parity, PROV and OpenLineage bounded-loss qualification, stable publication identifier, migration evidence and signed v1 attestation remain open.

tracks.scope: Adversarial review of the bounded lineage query envelope and change-impact evidence.
findings: The current query implementation and tests support bounded lineage and impact queries.
Stable API negotiation, authorization, pagination and performance envelopes, representative graph scale and external SDK consumption remain unqualified.

tracks.scope: Adversarial review of resumable publication, prepublication verification and bounded synthetic publication packets.
findings: The pipeline has executable fail-closed publication and attestation checks for bounded artifacts.
External discovery and installation workflows, complete citation and preservation verification, correction lifecycle operation and stable publication qualification remain open.

tracks.scope: Adversarial review of bounded related-repository adapters and template conformance evidence.
findings: The fyi-cli and fyi-archive adapters preserve a bounded compatibility report without claiming universal adoption.
Broader repository migration, versioned template release, maintenance commitments and representative downstream upgrade evidence remain outstanding.

tracks.scope: Adversarial review of DNS pinning, attestation verification, threat policy, workflow controls and hosted-runner boundaries.
findings: The M1 controls include immutable action pins, least-privilege evidence workflows, threat and vulnerability policy, and bounded attestation verification.
Hosted release-environment verification, executed release SBOM and signing path, credential-compromise and rollback exercises, and final security panel disposition remain pending.

tracks.scope: Adversarial review of the synthetic simulation core, analysis protocol and clean-room benchmark preparation.
findings: The deterministic synthetic benchmark provides a reproducible implementation reference with explicit non-operational boundaries.
Domain simulation adapters, empirical calibration and validation, external benchmark comparison, performance qualification and real-world fitness remain open.

tracks.scope: Adversarial review of bounded feature-difference and temporal quality behavior.
findings: The current spatial difference implementation and tests provide bounded M1 evidence for declared semantics.
Representative national geometry and bitemporal quality measurements, uncertainty benchmarks, source-change histories and stable qualification are not present.

tracks.scope: Adversarial review of the synthetic supermarket-health envelope and bounded public-source intake.
findings: The synthetic methods core and intake records retain non-operational and source-status limitations.
Rights-cleared versioned supermarket inputs, baseline reproduction, accessibility and health analysis, planning alternatives, complete research objects and final panel qualification remain open.

tracks.scope: Adversarial review of the stable-v1 readiness baseline, agent-panel policy, hosted campaign design and release-decision boundaries.
findings: The repository now separates agent-panel qualification from external participant evidence, elapsed evidence and accountable release authority, and records remaining gates without promoting maturity.

Stable v1 is not qualified: all tracks remain M1, the elapsed beta and RC durations are incomplete, national-scale measurements and external participant workflows are absent, production disaster recovery is pending, and no accountable stable-release decision exists.

non_claims: This adversarial-agent report is one panel lens and is not an orchestrator synthesis or complete three-role panel disposition.
A pass-with-limitations disposition qualifies only the bounded evidence slice reviewed; it does not mark a track complete or advance its M1 maturity.
This report is not external operator or external user evidence and does not replace factual participant workflows required by the release policy.
This report does not create elapsed operational-cycle or release-candidate soak time.
This report does not establish national-scale performance, production disaster-recovery qualification, source authority or operational safety.
This report is not an accountable release-authority decision and does not authorize beta, release-candidate or stable-v1 promotion.
